lesson.one_point_room.title: One-Point Room
lesson.one_point_room.summary: Use a horizon, one vanishing point and converging edges to build a room with believable depth, then design the space your way.
lesson.one_point_room.step.horizon: Place the horizon first. The vanishing point is an anchor on that line, not a mark you need to hit perfectly.
lesson.one_point_room.help.horizon: Use the crosshair guide to locate the shared direction point. Keep your horizon broad and readable.
lesson.one_point_room.complete.horizon: The horizon and depth anchor are established.
lesson.one_point_room.step.edges: Send the room edges toward the same vanishing point. These converging lines create the depth structure.
lesson.one_point_room.help.edges: Follow the convergence guides from the corners toward the shared anchor. Compare direction rather than chasing exact pixels.
lesson.one_point_room.complete.edges: The room now has a clear perspective structure.
lesson.one_point_room.step.wall: Add the back wall and a simple opening. Notice how the smaller far wall sits inside the larger room shape.
lesson.one_point_room.help.wall: Use the back-wall guide to compare width, height and near-versus-far scale before refining the doorway.
lesson.one_point_room.complete.wall: The far wall gives the room a readable depth range.
lesson.one_point_room.step.furniture: Build one or two simple furniture masses. Let their depth edges point toward the same vanishing point.
lesson.one_point_room.help.furniture: Start with the front face, then use the perspective anchors to send depth edges backward. Near forms can appear larger than far forms.
lesson.one_point_room.complete.furniture: The furniture now shares the room's perspective system.
lesson.one_point_room.step.design: Now design the room for a purpose—studio, bedroom, game space, library or something invented. Add only the objects that support your idea.
lesson.one_point_room.help.design: Choose one room purpose first, then add decor or furniture that makes that idea clearer. You do not need to match the teacher room.
lesson.one_point_room.complete.drawing: You used one-point perspective as a tool and turned the structure into your own room design.
